control_issue.title: [Claude x Jules loop prod-c1] control: checkpoints and stop switch
control_issue.body:
Control issue of the Claude x Jules campaign prod-c1.

* Loop checkpoints are recorded here (no action needed).
* **Stop switch:** close this issue or add the label `loop-stop`. New Jules starts stop; running work continues. Reopen / remove the label to resume.
* Usage limits: a `claude-jules-quota v1` record here makes the loop wait for the reset.

This issue is not a task. Do not add the `jules` label to it.

signals.summary: claude_jules_live_adapter: git 'cannot lock ref' push rejection is misreported as an ambiguous outcome
signals.detail: `GitLiveClient._push` (automation/command_bus/claude_jules_live_adapter.py line 141) treats a push as a definite rejection only when the output matches `non-fast-forward|fetch first|stale info|already exists`. When two controllers push to the same branch at the same moment, git rejects the loser with `! <sha>:refs/heads/<branch> [remote rejected] (failed to update ref)` and `remote: error: cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/<branch>': is at <X> but expected <Y>`. That output does not match, so `_push` raises `RuntimeError(... outcome ambiguous ...)` instead of `PushRejected`, and `create()` cannot rebuild on the moved tip although git wrote nothing. Observed in the batch 27 two-clone race test; reproduced deterministically by feeding that exact output to `_push`.
evidence: automation/command_bus/claude_jules_live_adapter.py:141 rejection regex misses 'failed to update ref' / 'cannot lock ref ... but expected'

docs/evidence/claude-jules-production-mvp-20261010/batch27-production-mvp.md: observed '[remote rejected] (failed to update ref)' + 'cannot lock ref ... is at X but expected Y' in the local bare-git race
deterministic repro on main 4bb5cd7: _push with that porcelain output raises RuntimeError 'outcome ambiguous', not PushRejected
acceptance_criteria: GitLiveClient._push raises PushRejected (definitely nothing written) when git reports '[remote rejected] (failed to update ref)' together with 'cannot lock ref ... is at <X> but expected <Y>'
Output that is really unknown (no rejection flag, or an unrecognised error) still raises the ambiguous RuntimeError; a successful push is unchanged

A regression test in test_claude_jules_live_adapter.py feeds the exact observed porcelain output and asserts PushRejected, and create() then rebuilds on the moved tip without losing the other controller's commit
No other file changes; no existing test is removed, skipped or weakened

Left open and unchanged; their objective o1-windows-portability is not approved in prod-c1, so the planner skips them visibly.
